f.title: Use an alternative approach only if it satisfies applicable statutes and regulations
f.statement: An applicant can use an approach other than the one in this guidance if the approach satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations; to discuss an alternative approach, the applicant contacts the FDA staff responsible for implementing the guidance or, if they cannot be identified, calls the number on the title page.

f.title: Include reasons for any failure to complete a commitment in the annual section 506B status report
f.statement: The annual report that section 506B of the Act requires the applicant to submit on the status of each postmarketing study subject to section 506B (agreed-upon commitments and required studies, including clinical trials) must also include the reasons, if any, for failure to complete the commitment; the provision is implemented at 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(vii) and 601.70.

f.applicability: Postmarketing studies and clinical trials subject to section 506B reporting

This provision is implemented at 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(vii) and 601.70.

f.title: Report annually on postmarketing studies that are not 506B studies (NDA applicants)
f.statement: NDA applicants are required by 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(viii) to report annually to FDA on postmarketing studies or trials that are not 506B studies or trials, such as CMC commitments and product stability studies agreed with FDA, and any other postmarketing study not included under 314.81(b)(2)(vii) that is being performed by, or on behalf of, the applicant; these are not reports required under section 506B.
f.topic: Annual report on other postmarketing studies
f.applicability: NDA applicants; non-506B postmarketing studies and trials (CMC commitments, stability studies, other studies performed by or on behalf of the applicant)

rows.actor: NDA applicant
rows.quote: In addition, new drug application (NDA) applicants are required by 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(viii) to report annually to FDA on postmarketing studies or trials that are not 506B studies or trials. Such studies or trials are not required, and they include chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) studies that applicants have agreed with FDA to conduct (CMC commitments), and all product stability studies that applicants have agreed with FDA to conduct (stability studies). The reporting requirement at 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(viii) also includes “any postmarketing study not included under [§ 314.81](b)(2)(vii) . . . that is being performed by, or on behalf of, the applicant.” Reports on the status of these types of studies are not reports required under section 506B.

f.title: Classify postmarketing investigations as clinical trials or studies
f.statement: For implementing section 901 of FDAAA, clinical trials are any prospective investigations in which the applicant or investigator determines the method of assigning the drug product(s) or other interventions to one or more human subjects; studies are all other investigations, such as investigations with humans that are not clinical trials (e.g., observational epidemiologic studies), animal studies and laboratory experiments.
f.clause: II.B.1. FDA May Require Applicants to Conduct Studies and Clinical Trials
f.exceptions: These definitions do not affect whether the trials or studies are subject to Title VIII of FDAAA (Clinical Trial Databases) and section 402(j) of the PHS Act (footnote 12).

f.title: Provide a timetable for completion for every required postmarketing study and clinical trial

f.title: Design observational pharmacoepidemiologic PMR studies with protocol, control group and prespecified hypotheses

f.clause: III.A. Examples of Postmarketing Requirements (PMRs) Under Section 505(o) - Observational pharmacoepidemiologic studies
f.applicability: Observational pharmacoepidemiologic studies required as PMRs
f.exceptions: Control groups may be omitted when there is a scientifically valid reason; descriptive studies may use stated objectives instead of a prespecified hypothesis (see separate rows).

f.title: Voluntary registries may be used for a later-required PMR study
f.statement: A sponsor may voluntarily create a registry to serve as a repository for clinical data, such as an outcomes registry; such a registry is not required as part of a PMR, but if FDA becomes aware of new safety information in the post approval setting, the sponsor could be required to conduct a PMR study, which may utilize the registry data.

f.title: Set the final protocol submission date to allow for FDA protocol discussion
f.statement: For PMRs and PMCs the first milestone is generally the final protocol submission date; final implies the applicant has submitted a protocol, the FDA review team has commented and the protocol has been revised as needed, so the date for this milestone should be selected to allow for the discussion period needed to create a well-designed study or clinical trial.

f.statement: For studies or clinical trials otherwise undertaken by the applicant to investigate a safety issue (neither required by nor agreed with FDA, and possibly initiated without prior discussion with or notification to FDA), the applicant must report to FDA under section 505(o)(3)(E)(ii) and 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(viii); these studies and clinical trials must be summarized in a section of the annual report (drugs) or annual status report (biologics).

f.title: Describe PMRs and safety studies in REMS assessments without submitting PMRs as part of the REMS
f.statement: Section 505-1(g)(3)(B) and (C) requires that REMS assessments include the status of postapproval studies and clinical trials required under section 505(o) and those otherwise undertaken to investigate a safety issue; PMRs are not part of REMS and are not submitted as part of the REMS, but must be described in REMS assessments.

f.statement: Applicants can satisfy the REMS assessment status requirements by referring to relevant information in the most recent annual report required under section 506B and 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(vii) or 21 CFR 601.70, and including any material or significant updates to the status information since the annual report was prepared; failure to comply with the REMS assessment provisions in section 505-1(g) could result in enforcement action.

f.statement: When multiple related applications exist (e.g., several formulations of the same drug with the same applicant), unified reporting, consistent with past practice, may be considered; an applicant who proposes unified reporting should discuss the proposal with the review division.

f.title: Appeal a PMR through formal dispute resolution
f.statement: The applicant may appeal a requirement to conduct a postmarketing study or clinical trial using the usual dispute resolution procedures (guidance on Formal Dispute Resolution: Appeals Above the Division Level; section 505(o)(3)(F)).

f.title: Meet PMR timetable and periodic reporting requirements or show good cause
f.statement: An applicant's failure to comply with the timetable, periodic report submissions and other requirements of section 505(o)(3)(E)(ii) will be considered a violation unless the applicant demonstrates good cause for the noncompliance; FDA is authorized to determine what constitutes good cause.

f.title: Applicants violating postmarketing study requirements may face civil money penalties that double every 30 days after FDA notice
f.statement: Under section 303(f)(4)(A), an applicant that violates postmarketing study or clinical trial requirements may be subject to civil monetary penalties of up to $250,000 per violation and no more than $1 million for all violations adjudicated in a single proceeding. If the violation continues more than 30 days after FDA notifies the applicant, the penalty doubles for the following 30-day period and keeps doubling for each later 30-day period, up to $1 million per period and $10 million for all violations adjudicated in a single proceeding. In setting the amount, FDA considers the applicant's efforts to correct the violation (section 303(f)(4)(B)).
f.clause: VII. Enforcement of Requirements for Postmarketing Studies and Clinical Trials - Civil monetary penalties
f.exceptions: FDA considers the applicant's efforts to correct the violation in setting the amount

These penalties increase if the violation continues more than 30 days after FDA notifies the applicant of the violation. The penalties double for the following 30-day period and continue to double for subsequent 30-day periods, up to $1 million per period and $10 million for all violations adjudicated in a single proceeding. In determining the amount of a civil penalty, FDA will consider the applicant's efforts to correct the violation (see section 303(f)(4)(B) of the Act).
